::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jan 31st 1890  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Girton College Cambridge, Yonge IV 15
:::

Dear [Mr Innes](people/person_744.qmd)
Thank you much for what was useless trouble. I thought Stanford was sure to have had such maps reasonably cheap for travellers.[^1] There is a good little geological map of England in Letts’s [atlas](other_books/otherbook_629.qmd), but the book is very badly bound, and  that one map in my copy has some how been lost.

I think there are small editions of [Keith Johnstone](other_books/otherbook_628.qmd)- but his publisher is [Blackwood](organizations/other_214.qmd), I suppose he has an office in London but I do not know where. I am astonished at the expensiveness in these days of chromolithography  But unless Blackwood is near at hand, or you have a catalogue which would shew if [Cassell](organizations/other_216.qmd) has a cheap one, pray do not take any more trouble

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

Perhaps the best way would be to ask Blackwood and Cassell to send me a catalogue

---

[^1]: Edward Stanford opened a specialist map shop in 1853 which is still (2010) operating.
